user.title: Access Guard
user.description: Shows who is signed in to Home Assistant and from where, and lets an administrator sign out a single session.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Access Guard is already set up.

init.title: Access Guard options

data.home_wan_entity: Sensor holding the home's public IP (optional)
data.failures_before_login: Failed attempts before a login that alerts
data.persistent_notification: Show alerts as notifications in Home Assistant
data.burst_failures: Failed attempts that make a burst
data.allowed_countries: Countries that never alert as new
data.actionable: Offer "Sign out this login" on phone alerts

data_description.geo_path: Download dbip-country-lite CSV from db-ip.com and put it here. Without it, no country is shown. Nothing is looked up online.
data_description.home_wan_entity: Logins from this address are labelled 'home via internet' instead of 'internet'.
data_description.rules: Each alert also fires the access_guard_anomaly event, for your own automations.
data_description.failures_before_login: A login from an address that failed this many times in the 15 minutes before it. 1 also catches a single mistyped password.
data_description.sensitive_domains: A new login from outside the home whose first move, within 5 minutes, is a live camera view or an action on one of these.
data_description.persistent_notification: Notifications are visible to every account, like the sessions sensor.
data_description.notify_service: A notify action such as notify.mobile_app_pat_phone. A push leaves your instance through its provider (Google or Apple) carrying the person's name, address and, with the button, the login's handle.
data_description.burst_failures: Within 5 minutes, from one address, or from at least 3 addresses together.
data_description.allowed_countries: Two-letter codes, such as CZ. A person's first country is learnt silently either way.
data_description.actionable: Only with a mobile app notify action, and only for an alert about one exact login. The tap is checked like the sign-out action: the phone's person must be an administrator with a signed-in Home Assistant app.

init.description: Alerts notify. The only sign-out is one an administrator taps on their own phone.

error.invalid_notify_service: Enter a notify action, such as notify.mobile_app_pat_phone.
error.invalid_country: Use two-letter country codes, such as CZ.

sign_out.name: Sign out a session
sign_out.description: Ends one login (one app or browser) at once. The account stays active and its person can sign in again. Administrators only.

handle.name: Handle
handle.description: The 12-character handle of the login, from the sessions sensor.

sign_out_user.name: Sign out all of a person's sessions
sign_out_user.description: Ends every login of one person. The account stays active and they can sign in again. Administrators only.

user_id.name: User ID
user_id.description: The person's user id, from the sessions sensor.

unban.name: Lift an IP ban
unban.description: Removes one address from Home Assistant's IP bans (ip_bans.yaml) and resets its failed-login count. Administrators only.

ip.name: IP address
ip.description: The banned address, from the bans sensor.

options.login_after_failures: A login after failed attempts from its address
options.sensitive_first: A new outside login first watches a camera or opens a lock
options.long_lived_token: A long-lived access token is created
options.non_admin_internet: A person who is not an administrator signs in from the internet
options.new_country: A person uses a login from a country new for them
options.failed_login_burst: A burst of failed sign-in attempts

admin_without_mfa.title: {name} signs in without multi-factor authentication
admin_without_mfa.description: {name} is an administrator and can change everything in Home Assistant, but signs in with a password alone. Ask them to open their profile, then *Multi-factor authentication*, and enable it. This issue goes away by itself once they have; you can also ignore it.
